body.x: Marking its third edition this year, FIX 2026 (Future Innovation Tech Expo), South Korea’s benchmark future industry exhibition, will be held from Wednesday, October 21 to Saturday, October 24 at EXCO in Daegu. Under the slogan “AI, Beyond Tech into Reality,” the expo establishes a new milestone for global industry by organically linking core technologies across four key advanced sectors: future mobility, robotics, AI and ICT, and startups. Encompassing the achievements of Daegu Metropolitan City’s forward-looking industrial cultivation, leading domestic and international tech enterprises alongside promising startups will assemble to unveil next-generation, field-validated technologies poised to transform everyday life and industrial operations. Concurrently featuring international conferences, global business matchmaking sessions, and open innovation initiatives, the event is set to serve as a pivotal exchange hub leading technological collaboration and innovation far beyond Asia.

Participating as an official Global Media Award partner for FIX 2026, Otaku Soken is a unique Japanese media organization that organically integrates entertainment sectors such as anime and gaming with advanced technology, business, and economics. From innovative hardware enabling immersive content—such as gaming gear, smart glasses, and extended reality (XR) devices—to industrial applications of generative AI, the outlet commands a dedicated readership of tech enthusiasts and industry executives through its distinctive editorial perspective. It has earned widespread recognition for in-depth journalism that balances technical excellence with cultural impact and copyright ethics within entertainment. Leveraging its reporting expertise across global tech ecosystems in North America, Europe, and Asia, Otaku Soken plans to vividly introduce Japanese audiences to South Korea’s innovative hardware and tech startups. An advance interview was conducted with Tomoki Yoshioka, Editor-in-Chief of Otaku Soken, to discuss the convergence of digital content and technology and his expectations for FIX 2026.

body.cap: Screenshot of Otaku Soken's main page

body.x: Q1. Could you introduce your media outlet to readers?

Otaku Soken is a unique concept in Japan, a specialized media publication that converges entertainment domains such as animation and gaming with technology and economics. For instance, dedicated gaming devices are essential to playing video games, while smart glasses offer practical convenience for enjoying anime on a massive virtual display. ACG (Anime, Comics, Games) content exchanges are exceptionally vibrant in South Korea, with major conventions like G-STAR, making this editorial focus feel very natural and approachable to Korean audiences.
Q2. What are your perspectives on current trends across industrial technology, mobility, and AI?

Regarding mobility, particularly electric vehicles (EVs), significant insights have been gathered through global event coverage such as CES, where China’s rapid rise is especially noticeable. Cross-industry entry into the automotive sector has been prominent recently, yet market dynamics appear to be shifting amid intensifying competitive pressure. Noteworthy examples include Sony Honda Mobility in Japan and Dreame’s decision in China to discontinue its automotive venture, and it will be compelling to observe whether these adjustments continue.

In artificial intelligence, approaching the domain from an entertainment media standpoint requires handling ethical considerations more deliberately and cautiously than conventional tech media. Japanese legal frameworks maintain relatively lenient regulations on the use of copyrighted works for AI model training, leading to a polarization between regulatory advocates and proponents of promotion, especially in the illustration and video sectors. Rather than being confined to rigid ideological camps, the essential role is to report continuously on technical progress while maintaining awareness of these complex ethical questions.
Q3. What key themes or topics related to FIX 2026 will interest your readership most?

The publication places significant emphasis on “gadgets that surprise consumers,” an editorial focus that consistently draws strong reader engagement. Infusing hardware with unprecedented, inventive ideas aligns closely with an “otaku” creative impulse, and spotlighting manufacturers who embody that spirit is a core mission. In addition to artificial intelligence, robust interest and demand continue to surround gaming hardware, augmented reality (AR), and virtual reality (VR) technologies.
Q4. As this is your first time attending FIX, what are your primary expectations?

Having focused field investigations primarily on North America, Europe, and China, visiting a technology expo in South Korea is a rare opportunity. There is substantial anticipation for conducting on-the-ground research into the latest consumer and technological trends within the Korean market.
Q5. What are your thoughts on joining the Global Media Awards as an official partner?

Technology and entertainment represent domains where economic and cultural collaboration between South Korea and Japan has grown increasingly robust, making participation as an official partner an honor. By leveraging insights gained across Japanese and global markets, the objective is to contribute meaningfully to South Korea’s innovation journey while fully engaging with the exhibition program.
Meanwhile, ten prominent global media partners spanning Europe, the Americas, and Asia are participating as official press partners for FIX 2026, deploying on-site reporting delegations.

The international press corps includes leading technology and industry media representing their respective regions: Le Café du Geek, a French IT, lifestyle, and global tech publication; Clipset, a pioneering Spanish mobile and consumer tech outlet; Ubergizmo, a Silicon Valley-based American consumer electronics and innovative tech portal; AVING USA, an American global tech, business, and exhibition media outlet; Otaku Soken, a Japanese subculture and AI, VR, and IT convergence publication; DIGITIMES, world-renowned semiconductor and ICT supply chain media and research agency; VietnamPlus, a state-run multinational comprehensive news portal in Vietnam; ChinaByte, China’s first enterprise digital transformation (DX), IT, and AI publication; ET Manufacturing, an Indian smart factory, robotics, and manufacturing engineering media outlet; and Pokde.net, a Malaysian hardware, gaming, and mobile tech publication.

These global media partners will participate directly in on-site evaluations during the event, including the FIX Innovation Awards press conference and the Global Media Selected Best of FIX 2026 Media Awards, reporting from the front lines of technological developments by innovative enterprises shaping the future of South Korea’s high-tech landscape.
